title: Measurement: the WMI-free process table under the enforced deadline
summary: Supplemental to ACC-0081, and it does not replace EVD-0088 or EVD-0109, which stand as written. WMI IS GONE FROM THE WINDOWS IDENTITY ROUTE. F122: in run 35097288227 the PRIMED CIM read exceeded the 10,000 ms launch preflight bound and the launch refused before either child was spawned, which is the event EVD-0109 recorded as the trigger for removing WMI wholesale. The table is now read with NtQuerySystemInformation, called from PowerShell through reflection emit: no WMI, no compiler, one snapshot carrying every process's pid, parent pid and creation FILETIME without opening any process. Measured locally against the CIM route it replaced: about 300 ms a read against about 380 ms, 283 rows with NO missing creation times where Toolhelp32 could not read 160 of 291 without elevation, parent ids equal on 282 of 282 rows and every creation time within 1 microsecond. THE FINAL RUN IS 35294728144, all four cells green, 1,203 tests and 0 failures in each. Its six Windows records are complete true, withinBudget true, unfinished empty and notObserved empty, spending 5,877 to 6,979 ms of 8,000; the launch preflight cost 465 to 691 ms and read 141 to 149 rows, against 3,057 and 3,142 ms for the cold CIM preflights in run 35086096358. The six Linux records are complete true within 5,119 to 6,240 ms and run no preflight. F133, a unit test that injected its processes but computed its allowances from the wall clock, failed twice on loaded Windows runners by turning a survivor into an identity read the deadline refused; all four teardown tests that assert a survivor now fix their budget with their own clock, their waits unchanged, and the survivor mutations still fail every one of them. F130 IS INSTRUMENTED AND OPEN: each real read now records request, child created, first stdout and stderr byte, exit, timeout, kill request and close, with the child's pid, its exit code or signal and byte counts, and after a real timeout three sequential probes isolate PowerShell starting, the native call being defined and the query. Run 35253655887 caught one stall with that instrument: the child existed after 7.2 ms and wrote nothing at all for the full bound. Nothing stalled in the final run, so the probes did not fire and the phase breakdown is still unknown.

omissions.reason: F130 REMAINS INTERMITTENT AND UNEXPLAINED. It appeared in runs 35214314607, 35250274939 and 35253655887 and not in the three runs since. The one instrumented stall shows the silence begins after PowerShell exists and before its first byte; whether that is PowerShell's own startup, a scan of the script, or the native call itself is not distinguished. A green run does not close it.
The companions run only after a real timeout, and nothing timed out in the final run, so no phase breakdown was captured there.
The reader chooses its field offsets by pointer size. Only the 64-bit branch has ever run; the 32-bit branch is covered by a mutation, not by a 32-bit platform.

The parent pid sits in a region winternl.h marks reserved, and the call is defined in memory at runtime. Both were accepted deliberately: the layout has been stable since NT and is what Toolhelp32 reads, and a scanner that blocked the definition would make the reader fail closed.
MW1-MW7, MB1-MB4 and MA1-MA2 ran locally on Windows against node v24.18.0, not in CI.
CI runs ubuntu-latest and windows-latest only. Nothing here was observed on macOS.
